Entire Brain
============

[](#entire-brain)

Every developer builds on what came before: code written, ideas discussed, lessons learned, decisions made, feedback received, and failures understood. Our agents are trained on the world’s knowledge, but they lack the memory of how our projects got here. Entire Brain brings that experience forward, giving agents the context they need to start informed and build on prior work.

Entire Brain combines captured agent sessions and checkpoints with durable facts, documentation, and code understanding from [Entire Graph](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph). Graph maps how the code fits together; Brain connects that structure to why it exists, what happened before, and how to approach similar work.

Through the CLI, agents can retrieve earlier decisions, revisit past attempts and their outcomes, assemble context for a task, and turn reviewed lessons into reusable skills. Knowledge stays linked to its supporting evidence, so it can be checked, revised, and applied as the project evolves.

What to ask
-----------

[](#what-to-ask)

Ask your coding agent in plain language.

| Goal | Example prompt |

| Start a task | What should I know before changing the retry policy? |
| Recover a past decision | Why did we remove the queue abstraction? |
| Find what we already know | What do we know about retry limits? |
| Search past sessions and docs | Where did we discuss backpressure? |
| Understand the project | Summarize this project's structure and conventions. |
| Check saved facts | Check whether the sources for our saved facts still match the repository. |
| Inspect memory health | Which sources are missing or out of date? |

Directly: `entire brain brief "<task>"` to start a task, `recall "<question>"` for decisions and saved facts, `query "<text>"` for prose search across sessions, docs and history, `overview` for the project, `verify` to re-check fact sources, and `status` for memory health.

Facts are stored per branch. `recall` on a branch that has no facts prints nothing and adds a note that every captured session is already distilled — which reads as "the brain does not know", not "you are on the wrong branch"; pass `--branch main` (or the branch the work happened on) before concluding anything.

Features
--------

[](#features)

*   Give an agent relevant decisions, code locations, and suggested tests before it starts a task.
*   Save project facts by hand or extract them from past sessions, then check their source references against the repository.
*   Search facts, history, documentation, and conversations by keyword or meaning.
*   Find code, inspect the impact of a change, and investigate regressions with [Entire Graph](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph).
*   Connect agents through the CLI, with response size limits and repository instructions.
*   Browse saved knowledge in a terminal dashboard or an offline graph view.
*   Record facts globally, not just per repository, so a preference or team convention applies everywhere.
*   Read the documents that are not code: PDFs, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files under `docs/`.
*   Notify CI, a chat channel, or an index with signed webhooks when the brain changes.
*   Brain reads sessions captured by Entire CLI and uses Entire Graph for code analysis. Without captured sessions, Brain builds from code, docs, and Git history.
*   Graph is required for code analysis, but you can use Brain to search sessions, docs, and facts without it.

Install
-------

[](#install)

# Entire CLI — captures the agent sessions Brain learns from.
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash

# Brain.
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/entireio/entire-brain/main/scripts/get-brain.sh | bash

# Graph — the code analysis Brain builds on.
entire plugin install graph

The script downloads a prebuilt binary for your platform, checks it against the release checksums, and registers it with the CLI as the `entire brain` plugin. There is nothing to compile. Pin a release with `--version vX.Y.Z`, take the current prerelease with `--nightly`, or install somewhere other than `~/.local/bin` with `--dir`.

Without Graph, `setup` reports the semantic index as unavailable; sessions, docs and facts still work. Without the CLI there are no sessions to read, and Brain falls back to code, docs and Git history.

Building from source

Needs Go 1.27.3+, Git 2.36+, the Entire CLI on `PATH`, and a C compiler for Graph's tree-sitter bindings.

git clone https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain.git
cd entire-brain
./scripts/install.sh

Builds and registers Brain and Graph. It does not initialize a repository's memory or install the watcher.

The clone is itself a git repository, and `setup` acts on the repository you run it in. Go back to your own project's directory before you run `entire brain setup`, or pass the project's path as an argument.

See [installation options](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/operations.md#full-install) for choosing a Graph checkout, installing offline, or building Brain alone.

### Transcript storage and version compatibility

[](#transcript-storage-and-version-compatibility)

The storage change introduced in [#392](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/392) makes persistent brains read transcripts from local Git checkpoint refs instead of keeping exported transcript files. Existing file-based brains and standalone bundles remain readable. On the next persistent session refresh, Brain verifies that legacy cached transcripts can be recovered from local checkpoints before removing them. If recovery cannot be proven, refresh fails and retains the cache.

| Scenario | Compatibility |

| Upgrade an existing file-based brain | Supported; migration checks recovery before deleting cached transcripts. |
| Read a materialized bundle with an older binary | Supported when the older binary supports the bundle's schema. |
| Run an older binary against a migrated persistent brain | Not supported. Current memory and manifest schemas require the upgraded binary. |

Upgrade and restart all Brain CLI and watcher processes that share a brain before migrating it. Installing or upgrading Graph does not upgrade Brain.

Local memory migration is one-way. A post-migration bundle is not a downgrade format. To use an older release, restore a complete pre-migration backup into a separate environment. That backup does not include later writes. See [memory storage compatibility](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/memory-storage-compatibility.md) before upgrading.

### How Brain compares

[](#how-brain-compares)

[`docs/feature-matrix.md`](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/feature-matrix.md) — 51 capabilities against five alternatives, including the 18 rows where neither Graph nor Brain answers Yes. Our columns are read from the binaries; the competitor columns are not.

Every number we publish, how to reproduce it, and what we deliberately do not claim: [benchmarks](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md).

Activate it for your agent
--------------------------

[](#activate-it-for-your-agent)

For Claude capture, follow the [capture requirements](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/memory-storage-compatibility.md#claude-capture-requirement).

Brain is set up per [repository](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/reference.md#3a-what-setup-needs-first-and-what-it-does-not). Start in a local Git repository with at least one commit:

entire brain setup

By default, `setup` indexes the repository, extracts facts from up to 25 past sessions in the background, installs a watcher to keep the memory updated, and installs the agent instructions. The watcher runs as a persistent service on macOS and Linux with systemd.

The agent instructions live in these files, created or updated by `setup`:

*   `.entire/agent-guide.md`: the agent instructions. Rerunning setup replaces this file.
*   `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`: references to the guide inside managed blocks. Your text outside those blocks is preserved.

The guide is assembled from whichever products have been **activated**, and each product activates itself. `entire brain setup` on its own writes a Brain-only guide containing no Graph instructions at all — installing Graph does not change that, because activation is recorded in the guide rather than probed. Run `entire graph setup` too if you want both.

The two setups compose in **either order**. The guide text is mirrored between the two products, so both render the same combined guide; each run only adds its own product to the recorded activation.

Review the generated files and commit them together when the instructions should apply to your team. Restart your agent or reload its repository instructions so it picks up the guide.

See the [agent integration guide](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/reference.md#how-agents-use-the-brain) and [coordination contract](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/agent-coordination.md) for more setup details.

### Brain without fact extraction

[](#brain-without-fact-extraction)

Extracting facts uses an available agent CLI and can send session content to its model provider and incur token charges. Without an agent CLI, this step is skipped.

To build without fact extraction or a background service, use:

entire brain setup --no-backfill --no-daemon

Configured remote history sources and hosted memories sync also use the network; see [privacy and egress](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/reference.md#privacy-and-egress) for controls.

### Background maintenance and memory sync

[](#background-maintenance-and-memory-sync)

The watcher updates local repository context and runs distillation within the configured budget. For connected repositories, Brain syncs after a post-commit checkpoint notification and after distillation saves its results. Existing push notifications and manual sync remain supported. The watcher does not upload or pull memories on idle ticks. Brain no longer processes session-end notifications.

Sync sends new or changed record versions and saves server acknowledgements locally. Overlapping uploads use one process lock; successful batches do not need another upload. Failed or interrupted uploads remain eligible for the next sync event. Original session, checkpoint, and commit references remain unchanged.

Usage Examples
--------------

[](#usage-examples)

### Check what the brain knows

[](#check-what-the-brain-knows)

# One-line health and coverage summary.
entire brain status

# The full picture: sources, freshness, blind spots.
entire brain status --verbose

# What is this project? Stack, boundaries, commands, recent decisions.
entire brain overview

### Record and retrieve facts (episodic memory)

[](#record-and-retrieve-facts-episodic-memory)

# Author a durable fact about this repository.
entire brain remember "Retries are capped at 3; the 4th failure must page."

# Retrieve facts for the current branch (--branch <name> for another).
entire brain recall "retry policy"

# Re-check every fact's anchors against the current tree.
entire brain verify

`remember` infers where the fact belongs using a coding agent on `PATH`. Without one, pass it yourself: `--path constraints.retry.policy`, shaped `category.subcategory.type`, from `architecture`, `constraints`, `preferences`, `project`, `workflow`. Segments use lowercase letters, digits and `_`; a hyphen is rejected.

`verify` reports hand-written facts as `unverifiable-here` — they have no source anchor in the repository. Expected, not a failure.

Memory access uses one repository API and one `facts/store.json` file (schema 3). Memories are visible across branches. Migration combines copies with the same ID and retains provenance and lifecycle state. Brainstore's per-record wire format remains unchanged.

Normal writes and refreshes migrate legacy stores automatically. Verified redundant `facts/.legacy-*` files are then removed automatically, including copies retained by v0.5.0. Watcher maintenance also runs when repository contents have not changed. No migration or cleanup command is required for normal operation.

Cleanup preserves unknown files and records whose preservation cannot be proved. Large-file verification runs outside the write lock; a concurrent change defers removal until another pass. Interrupted cleanup resumes automatically. Background pause settings remain effective, and ordinary reads never migrate or clean up.

Storage diagnostics are available when needed:

entire brain memories storage status --json
entire brain memories storage migrate       # optional diagnostic/retry operation

Both commands accept `--global`. Status includes cleanup state, pending legacy directories, retained reasons, and recorded reclaimed bytes. A crash after removal can make the byte count an underestimate; it does not authorize deletion.

Local migration is one-way. Stable v0.2.0, v0.3.0, and v0.4.0 cannot read the migrated directory. Older and newer clients can exchange hosted memories through separate local stores. Returning to an older version requires a complete pre-migration backup in a separate environment; later writes are not in that backup. Do not share a migrated local directory with older clients.

Run `bash scripts/test-memory-storage-compat.sh` for released-binary checks. The script builds pinned stable releases v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.4.0, and v0.5.0. Nightly releases are excluded. Tests use temporary repositories and isolated stores. They do not change your installed plugin or your memories. See [compatibility coverage](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/memory-storage-compatibility.md) for test scope.

### Remember something that is not about one repository

[](#remember-something-that-is-not-about-one-repository)

Most facts belong to a codebase. Some — a preference, a team convention, where the staging cluster lives — are true in every repository you work in, and had nowhere to live but one repo's brain.

entire brain remember "The staging cluster is in eu-west-1." --global
entire brain facts global                  # everything recorded globally
entire brain facts retract <id\> --global

Global facts are recalled from every repository on the machine that recorded them and labelled `(global)` when they surface, so a general convention is never mistaken for something this codebase declared. `memories sync` does not upload them, so another machine does not see them. `--no-global`, or `ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_GLOBAL_FACTS=1`, leaves them out.

Running `remember` outside a checkout records the fact globally instead of failing — which is usually where you are when the thing you want to write down is not about one repo.

### Search

[](#search)

# BM25 lexical ranking across facts, history, and docs.
entire brain query "why did we drop the queue abstraction"

Semantic (embedding) retrieval was removed: a 1,748-run agent eval measured BM25 lexical ranking matching or beating the embedder stack end-to-end while cutting agent tokens 18-28%, query memory 96%, and 31 MB off the binary (see docs/eval\_ledger.md and trail #278). `--keyword` is accepted for compatibility (it is the only mode); `--semantic` and `vsearch` run the same BM25 ranking and print a stderr notice.

Supply the query text positionally or with `--query`; flags can appear before or after it:

entire brain query --keyword --query "RetryPolicy"

Supplying both a positional query and `--query` is an error. The same forms work with `entire brain workspace query <workspace>`.

`query` also takes `--source` (`all` | `fact` | `history` | `doc` | `conversation`) to narrow the corpus, and `--json` for machine-readable output:

entire brain query "auth middleware" --source fact --json | jq '.results\[0\]'

### Read documents that are not code

[](#read-documents-that-are-not-code)

A design doc written in Word, a spec that arrived as a PDF, a requirements matrix in a spreadsheet — put them in `docs/` and `refresh` reads them into the brain alongside markdown, so they come back from `search` and `brief` like anything else.

entire brain docs extract docs/spec.pdf # what it will get out of one file

Extraction is deterministic and local: no model, no network, no external tools, no OCR. A scanned PDF has no text layer, and Brain says so rather than indexing an empty document:

    docs/scanned-form.pdf: the PDF has no text layer
      (it is probably a scan; OCR is out of scope for this build)
    

Fact text from documents is indexed as-is; see [documents](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/reference.md#documents) for what is read from each format and what is left out.

### Navigate the code semantically

[](#navigate-the-code-semantically)

# What does changing this symbol affect?
entire brain inspect impact --symbol ValidateToken

# What is unreachable?
entire brain inspect dead-code --json

# What changed since the brain was last indexed?
entire brain inspect changes

### Build a task packet for an agent

[](#build-a-task-packet-for-an-agent)

# A bounded context packet scoped to one task.
entire brain brief "add rate limiting to the upload endpoint"

### Explore the brain interactively

[](#explore-the-brain-interactively)

entire brain dash   # TUI: status, facts, sessions, history, semantic
entire brain viz    # offline graph in your browser

[![entire brain viz — a walkthrough of the five sections of a brain](/entireio/entire-brain/raw/main/docs/images/brain-viz.gif)](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/images/brain-viz.gif)

`viz` opens the whole brain as one graph and lets you walk into each part of it: **semantic** (functions, types and calls), **facts** (decisions, gotchas and rules), **sessions** (agents, turns and work), **history** (commits and checkpoints) and **docs** (seed, guides and context). The recording above is a real brain — 20,478 symbols, 807,186 history records, 2,375 sessions — and it runs entirely on your machine: no network, no model calls, read-only.

### Notify another service when the brain changes

[](#notify-another-service-when-the-brain-changes)

Point Brain at an HTTP endpoint and it posts a small JSON event when a fact is recorded or retracted, or the brain is refreshed — so a CI job, a chat channel, or an index can react without polling.

export ENTIRE\_BRAIN\_WEBHOOK\_URL=https://hooks.example.com/entire
export ENTIRE\_BRAIN\_WEBHOOK\_SECRET=a-long-random-string

entire brain webhook test     # prove the endpoint works
entire brain webhook events   # fact.recorded, fact.retracted, brain.refreshed

Events carry the fact's id, kind, and taxonomy paths — not its text, unless you set `ENTIRE_BRAIN_WEBHOOK_INCLUDE_TEXT=1`. With a secret set, each POST is signed with HMAC-SHA256 in `X-Entire-Signature-256`. Unset the URL and nothing is sent. See [webhooks](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/reference.md#webhooks).

### Recover from a split brain

[](#recover-from-a-split-brain)

A repository reached through two different paths — a symlink, or `/tmp` on macOS — could once end up with two brains and then refuse every repo-scoped command. Keys are now derived from the resolved directory, so new splits cannot happen; if you have an existing one:

# List every store this repository resolves to.
entire brain repo-identity

# Keep one and retire the others (renamed to a dated sibling, never deleted).
entire brain repo-identity --keep <repo-key\>

Stored memory and freshness
---------------------------

[](#stored-memory-and-freshness)

Brain's code index can fall behind your working tree. The watcher updates it automatically; run `entire brain refresh` to update it manually. Graph's interactive queries normally read the current working tree directly.

Run `entire brain verify` to check whether a fact's source references still match the repository.

`entire brain path` prints where this repository's memory is stored. See [storage and configuration](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/reference.md#storage-and-configuration) to change storage locations or search settings.

To stop and remove the watcher, run `entire brain setup --uninstall-daemon`. See [operations](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/operations.md#after-the-install-onboard-a-repository) for service management.

Limitations
-----------

[](#limitations)

Facts extracted by a model can be wrong. Check the linked sources before relying on them. `brain verify` checks source references, not whether a conclusion is correct.

Code analysis inherits Graph's limitations: dynamic calls can go unresolved, and parsing support varies by language.

The historical scale benchmark measured a 1.2 GB index and roughly 12-second median code search on one 4.8M-line repository. Those runs do not establish a scaling law or performance at 100M lines. See [scale](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/scale.md) for the measurements, their limits, and the command to benchmark a current build.

Search support varies by build and source. Check `entire brain capabilities` for available retrieval modes and the [conversation recall documentation](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/recall-evidence.md) for experimental features.

See the [recall threat model](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/recall_threat_model.md) for how Brain handles untrusted session content and retained secrets.

Entire Brain
============

[](#entire-brain)

Every developer builds on what came before: code written, ideas discussed, lessons learned, decisions made, feedback received, and failures understood. Our agents are trained on the world’s knowledge, but they lack the memory of how our projects got here. Entire Brain brings that experience forward, giving agents the context they need to start informed and build on prior work.

Entire Brain combines captured agent sessions and checkpoints with durable facts, documentation, and code understanding from [Entire Graph](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph). Graph maps how the code fits together; Brain connects that structure to why it exists, what happened before, and how to approach similar work.

Through the CLI, agents can retrieve earlier decisions, revisit past attempts and their outcomes, assemble context for a task, and turn reviewed lessons into reusable skills. Knowledge stays linked to its supporting evidence, so it can be checked, revised, and applied as the project evolves.

What to ask
-----------

[](#what-to-ask)

Ask your coding agent in plain language.

| Goal | Example prompt |

| Start a task | What should I know before changing the retry policy? |
| Recover a past decision | Why did we remove the queue abstraction? |
| Find what we already know | What do we know about retry limits? |
| Search past sessions and docs | Where did we discuss backpressure? |
| Understand the project | Summarize this project's structure and conventions. |
| Check saved facts | Check whether the sources for our saved facts still match the repository. |
| Inspect memory health | Which sources are missing or out of date? |

Directly: `entire brain brief "<task>"` to start a task, `recall "<question>"` for decisions and saved facts, `query "<text>"` for prose search across sessions, docs and history, `overview` for the project, `verify` to re-check fact sources, and `status` for memory health.

Facts are stored per branch. `recall` on a branch that has no facts prints nothing and adds a note that every captured session is already distilled — which reads as "the brain does not know", not "you are on the wrong branch"; pass `--branch main` (or the branch the work happened on) before concluding anything.

Features
--------

[](#features)

*   Give an agent relevant decisions, code locations, and suggested tests before it starts a task.
*   Save project facts by hand or extract them from past sessions, then check their source references against the repository.
*   Search facts, history, documentation, and conversations by keyword or meaning.
*   Find code, inspect the impact of a change, and investigate regressions with [Entire Graph](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph).
*   Connect agents through the CLI, with response size limits and repository instructions.
*   Browse saved knowledge in a terminal dashboard or an offline graph view.
*   Record facts globally, not just per repository, so a preference or team convention applies everywhere.
*   Read the documents that are not code: PDFs, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files under `docs/`.
*   Notify CI, a chat channel, or an index with signed webhooks when the brain changes.
*   Brain reads sessions captured by Entire CLI and uses Entire Graph for code analysis. Without captured sessions, Brain builds from code, docs, and Git history.
*   Graph is required for code analysis, but you can use Brain to search sessions, docs, and facts without it.

Install
-------

[](#install)

# Entire CLI — captures the agent sessions Brain learns from.
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash

# Brain.
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/entireio/entire-brain/main/scripts/get-brain.sh | bash

# Graph — the code analysis Brain builds on.
entire plugin install graph

The script downloads a prebuilt binary for your platform, checks it against the release checksums, and registers it with the CLI as the `entire brain` plugin. There is nothing to compile. Pin a release with `--version vX.Y.Z`, take the current prerelease with `--nightly`, or install somewhere other than `~/.local/bin` with `--dir`.

Without Graph, `setup` reports the semantic index as unavailable; sessions, docs and facts still work. Without the CLI there are no sessions to read, and Brain falls back to code, docs and Git history.

Building from source

Needs Go 1.27.3+, Git 2.36+, the Entire CLI on `PATH`, and a C compiler for Graph's tree-sitter bindings.

git clone https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain.git
cd entire-brain
./scripts/install.sh

Builds and registers Brain and Graph. It does not initialize a repository's memory or install the watcher.

The clone is itself a git repository, and `setup` acts on the repository you run it in. Go back to your own project's directory before you run `entire brain setup`, or pass the project's path as an argument.

See [installation options](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/operations.md#full-install) for choosing a Graph checkout, installing offline, or building Brain alone.

### Transcript storage and version compatibility

[](#transcript-storage-and-version-compatibility)

The storage change introduced in [#392](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/392) makes persistent brains read transcripts from local Git checkpoint refs instead of keeping exported transcript files. Existing file-based brains and standalone bundles remain readable. On the next persistent session refresh, Brain verifies that legacy cached transcripts can be recovered from local checkpoints before removing them. If recovery cannot be proven, refresh fails and retains the cache.

| Scenario | Compatibility |

| Upgrade an existing file-based brain | Supported; migration checks recovery before deleting cached transcripts. |
| Read a materialized bundle with an older binary | Supported when the older binary supports the bundle's schema. |
| Run an older binary against a migrated persistent brain | Not supported. Current memory and manifest schemas require the upgraded binary. |

Upgrade and restart all Brain CLI and watcher processes that share a brain before migrating it. Installing or upgrading Graph does not upgrade Brain.

Local memory migration is one-way. A post-migration bundle is not a downgrade format. To use an older release, restore a complete pre-migration backup into a separate environment. That backup does not include later writes. See [memory storage compatibility](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/memory-storage-compatibility.md) before upgrading.

Activate it for your agent
--------------------------

[](#activate-it-for-your-agent)

For Claude capture, follow the [capture requirements](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/memory-storage-compatibility.md#claude-capture-requirement).

Brain is set up per [repository](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/reference.md#3a-what-setup-needs-first-and-what-it-does-not). Start in a local Git repository with at least one commit:

entire brain setup

By default, `setup` indexes the repository, extracts facts from up to 25 past sessions in the background, installs a watcher to keep the memory updated, and installs the agent instructions. The watcher runs as a persistent service on macOS and Linux with systemd.

The agent instructions live in these files, created or updated by `setup`:

*   `.entire/agent-guide.md`: the agent instructions. Rerunning setup replaces this file.
*   `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`: references to the guide inside managed blocks. Your text outside those blocks is preserved.

The guide is assembled from whichever products have been **activated**, and each product activates itself. `entire brain setup` on its own writes a Brain-only guide containing no Graph instructions at all — installing Graph does not change that, because activation is recorded in the guide rather than probed. Run `entire graph setup` too if you want both.

The two setups compose in **either order**. The guide text is mirrored between the two products, so both render the same combined guide; each run only adds its own product to the recorded activation.

Review the generated files and commit them together when the instructions should apply to your team. Restart your agent or reload its repository instructions so it picks up the guide.

See the [agent integration guide](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/reference.md#how-agents-use-the-brain) and [coordination contract](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/agent-coordination.md) for more setup details.

### Brain without fact extraction

[](#brain-without-fact-extraction)

Extracting facts uses an available agent CLI and can send session content to its model provider and incur token charges. Without an agent CLI, this step is skipped.

To build without fact extraction or a background service, use:

entire brain setup --no-backfill --no-daemon

Configured remote history sources and hosted memories sync also use the network; see [privacy and egress](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/reference.md#privacy-and-egress) for controls.

### Background maintenance and memory sync

[](#background-maintenance-and-memory-sync)

The watcher updates local repository context and runs distillation within the configured budget. For connected repositories, Brain syncs after a post-commit checkpoint notification and after distillation saves its results. Existing push notifications and manual sync remain supported. The watcher does not upload or pull memories on idle ticks. Brain no longer processes session-end notifications.

Sync sends new or changed record versions and saves server acknowledgements locally. Overlapping uploads use one process lock; successful batches do not need another upload. Failed or interrupted uploads remain eligible for the next sync event. Original session, checkpoint, and commit references remain unchanged.

Usage Examples
--------------

[](#usage-examples)

### Check what the brain knows

[](#check-what-the-brain-knows)

# One-line health and coverage summary.
entire brain status

# The full picture: sources, freshness, blind spots.
entire brain status --verbose

# What is this project? Stack, boundaries, commands, recent decisions.

### Record and retrieve facts (episodic memory)

[](#record-and-retrieve-facts-episodic-memory)

# Author a durable fact about this repository.
entire brain remember "Retries are capped at 3; the 4th failure must page."

# Retrieve facts for the current branch (--branch <name> for another).
entire brain recall "retry policy"

# Re-check every fact's anchors against the current tree.
entire brain verify

`remember` infers where the fact belongs using a coding agent on `PATH`. Without one, pass it yourself: `--path constraints.retry.policy`, shaped `category.subcategory.type`, from `architecture`, `constraints`, `preferences`, `project`, `workflow`. Segments use lowercase letters, digits and `_`; a hyphen is rejected.

`verify` reports hand-written facts as `unverifiable-here` — they have no source anchor in the repository. Expected, not a failure.

Memory access uses one repository API and one `facts/store.json` file (schema 3). Memories are visible across branches. Migration combines copies with the same ID and retains provenance and lifecycle state. Brainstore's per-record wire format remains unchanged.

Normal writes and refreshes migrate legacy stores automatically. Verified redundant `facts/.legacy-*` files are then removed automatically, including copies retained by v0.5.0. Watcher maintenance also runs when repository contents have not changed. No migration or cleanup command is required for normal operation.

Cleanup preserves unknown files and records whose preservation cannot be proved. Large-file verification runs outside the write lock; a concurrent change defers removal until another pass. Interrupted cleanup resumes automatically. Background pause settings remain effective, and ordinary reads never migrate or clean up.

Storage diagnostics are available when needed:

entire brain memories storage status --json
entire brain memories storage migrate       # optional diagnostic/retry operation

Both commands accept `--global`. Status includes cleanup state, pending legacy directories, retained reasons, and recorded reclaimed bytes. A crash after removal can make the byte count an underestimate; it does not authorize deletion.

Local migration is one-way. Stable v0.2.0, v0.3.0, and v0.4.0 cannot read the migrated directory. Older and newer clients can exchange hosted memories through separate local stores. Returning to an older version requires a complete pre-migration backup in a separate environment; later writes are not in that backup. Do not share a migrated local directory with older clients.

Run `bash scripts/test-memory-storage-compat.sh` for released-binary checks. The script builds pinned stable releases v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.4.0, and v0.5.0. Nightly releases are excluded. Tests use temporary repositories and isolated stores. They do not change your installed plugin or your memories. See [compatibility coverage](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/memory-storage-compatibility.md) for test scope.

### Remember something that is not about one repository

[](#remember-something-that-is-not-about-one-repository)

Most facts belong to a codebase. Some — a preference, a team convention, where the staging cluster lives — are true in every repository you work in, and had nowhere to live but one repo's brain.

entire brain remember "The staging cluster is in eu-west-1." --global
entire brain facts global                  # everything recorded globally
entire brain facts retract <id\> --global

Global facts are recalled from every repository on the machine that recorded them and labelled `(global)` when they surface, so a general convention is never mistaken for something this codebase declared. `memories sync` does not upload them, so another machine does not see them. `--no-global`, or `ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_GLOBAL_FACTS=1`, leaves them out.

Running `remember` outside a checkout records the fact globally instead of failing — which is usually where you are when the thing you want to write down is not about one repo.

### Search

[](#search)

# BM25 lexical ranking across facts, history, and docs.
entire brain query "why did we drop the queue abstraction"

Semantic (embedding) retrieval was removed: a 1,748-run agent eval measured BM25 lexical ranking matching or beating the embedder stack end-to-end while cutting agent tokens 18-28%, query memory 96%, and 31 MB off the binary (see docs/eval\_ledger.md and trail #278). `--keyword` is accepted for compatibility (it is the only mode); `--semantic` and `vsearch` run the same BM25 ranking and print a stderr notice.

Supply the query text positionally or with `--query`; flags can appear before or after it:

entire brain query --keyword --query "RetryPolicy"

Supplying both a positional query and `--query` is an error. The same forms work with `entire brain workspace query <workspace>`.

`query` also takes `--source` (`all` | `fact` | `history` | `doc` | `conversation`) to narrow the corpus, and `--json` for machine-readable output:

entire brain query "auth middleware" --source fact --json | jq '.results\[0\]'

### Read documents that are not code

[](#read-documents-that-are-not-code)

A design doc written in Word, a spec that arrived as a PDF, a requirements matrix in a spreadsheet — put them in `docs/` and `refresh` reads them into the brain alongside markdown, so they come back from `search` and `brief` like anything else.

entire brain docs extract docs/spec.pdf # what it will get out of one file

Extraction is deterministic and local: no model, no network, no external tools, no OCR. A scanned PDF has no text layer, and Brain says so rather than indexing an empty document:

    docs/scanned-form.pdf: the PDF has no text layer
      (it is probably a scan; OCR is out of scope for this build)
    

Fact text from documents is indexed as-is; see [documents](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/reference.md#documents) for what is read from each format and what is left out.

[![entire brain viz — a walkthrough of the five sections of a brain](/entireio/entire-brain/raw/main/docs/images/brain-viz.gif)](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/images/brain-viz.gif)

`viz` opens the whole brain as one graph and lets you walk into each part of it: **semantic** (functions, types and calls), **facts** (decisions, gotchas and rules), **sessions** (agents, turns and work), **history** (commits and checkpoints) and **docs** (seed, guides and context). ### Notify another service when the brain changes

[](#notify-another-service-when-the-brain-changes)

Point Brain at an HTTP endpoint and it posts a small JSON event when a fact is recorded or retracted, or the brain is refreshed — so a CI job, a chat channel, or an index can react without polling.

export ENTIRE\_BRAIN\_WEBHOOK\_URL=https://hooks.example.com/entire
export ENTIRE\_BRAIN\_WEBHOOK\_SECRET=a-long-random-string

entire brain webhook test     # prove the endpoint works
entire brain webhook events   # fact.recorded, fact.retracted, brain.refreshed

Events carry the fact's id, kind, and taxonomy paths — not its text, unless you set `ENTIRE_BRAIN_WEBHOOK_INCLUDE_TEXT=1`. With a secret set, each POST is signed with HMAC-SHA256 in `X-Entire-Signature-256`. Unset the URL and nothing is sent. See [webhooks](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/reference.md#webhooks).

### Recover from a split brain

[](#recover-from-a-split-brain)

A repository reached through two different paths — a symlink, or `/tmp` on macOS — could once end up with two brains and then refuse every repo-scoped command. Keys are now derived from the resolved directory, so new splits cannot happen; if you have an existing one:

# List every store this repository resolves to.
entire brain repo-identity

# Keep one and retire the others (renamed to a dated sibling, never deleted).
entire brain repo-identity --keep <repo-key\>

Stored memory and freshness
---------------------------

[](#stored-memory-and-freshness)

Brain's code index can fall behind your working tree. The watcher updates it automatically; run `entire brain refresh` to update it manually. Graph's interactive queries normally read the current working tree directly.

Run `entire brain verify` to check whether a fact's source references still match the repository.

`entire brain path` prints where this repository's memory is stored. See [storage and configuration](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/reference.md#storage-and-configuration) to change storage locations or search settings.

To stop and remove the watcher, run `entire brain setup --uninstall-daemon`. See [operations](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/operations.md#after-the-install-onboard-a-repository) for service management.

Limitations
-----------

[](#limitations)

Facts extracted by a model can be wrong. Check the linked sources before relying on them. `brain verify` checks source references, not whether a conclusion is correct.

Code analysis inherits Graph's limitations: dynamic calls can go unresolved, and parsing support varies by language.

The historical scale benchmark measured a 1.2 GB index and roughly 12-second median code search on one 4.8M-line repository. Those runs do not establish a scaling law or performance at 100M lines. See [scale](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/scale.md) for the measurements, their limits, and the command to benchmark a current build.

Search support varies by build and source. Check `entire brain capabilities` for available retrieval modes and the [conversation recall documentation](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/recall-evidence.md) for experimental features.

See the [recall threat model](/entireio/entire-brain/blob/main/docs/recall_threat_model.md) for how Brain handles untrusted session content and retained secrets.

**Entire Brain** (`entireio/entire-brain`, MIT license) is a memory layer for a Git repository. It turns captured agent sessions, checkpoint history, docs, code structure, and durable facts into something you and your coding agents can query. Its goal is to give agents the project history they lack, such as past decisions, failed attempts, and why code exists. It works through a CLI (`entire brain ...`). It builds on **Entire Graph**, which handles code structure and analysis. Without captured sessions, Brain builds from code, docs, and Git history. Without Graph, sessions, docs, and facts still work, but code analysis is unavailable.

**Install** (three steps, per the README):

1. Entire CLI, which captures the sessions Brain learns from: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`
2. Brain: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/entireio/entire-brain/main/scripts/get-brain.sh | bash`
3. Graph: `entire plugin install graph`

The Brain script downloads a prebuilt binary, verifies it against release checksums, and registers it as the `entire brain` plugin. Its options are `--version vX.Y.Z` to pin a release, `--nightly` for the current prerelease, and `--dir` to change the install location from `~/.local/bin`. Since these are piped curl-to-bash commands, you may want to read the scripts first.

To build from source, you need Go 1.27.3+, Git 2.36+, the Entire CLI on `PATH`, and a C compiler. Then clone the repo and run `./scripts/install.sh`. That builds and registers Brain and Graph but does not set up a repository.

**Set up a repository:** run `entire brain setup` inside a local Git repo that has at least one commit. By default it indexes the repo, extracts facts from up to 25 past sessions in the background, installs a watcher (a persistent service on macOS and Linux with systemd), and writes agent instructions to `.entire/agent-guide.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `CLAUDE.md`. The README suggests reviewing and committing those files. Setup flags mentioned: `--no-backfill` (skip fact extraction), `--no-daemon` (no background service), and `--uninstall-daemon`. Fact extraction uses an agent CLI and may send session content to a model provider. Run `entire graph setup` too if you want Graph instructions in the agent guide.

**Commands the README names:**

- Status and overview: `status` (add `--verbose` for the full picture), `overview`, `doctor`, `stats`
- Context for a task: `brief "<task>"`
- Facts: `remember "<text>"` (add `--global` for facts that apply across repos), `recall "<question>"` (use `--branch <name>` for other branches), `verify`, `facts`, `distill`
- Search: `query "<text>"` (BM25 keyword ranking; supports `--source all|fact|history|doc|conversation` and `--json`), `get`, `multi-get`
- Code analysis (via Graph): `inspect impact --symbol <name>`, `inspect dead-code`, `inspect changes`
- Documents: `docs extract <file>` reads PDF, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files under `docs/`. Scanned PDFs without a text layer are not OCR'd.
- Interactive: `dash` (terminal dashboard), `viz` (offline graph in the browser)
- Upkeep: `refresh`, `watch`, `verify`, `stop`/`start`, `gc`, `reset`, `repair`, `path`, `repo-identity`
- Other: `webhook test|events` (notifications on fact or brain changes, via `ENTIRE_BRAIN_WEBHOOK_URL` and optional `ENTIRE_BRAIN_WEBHOOK_SECRET`), `workspace`, `bundle`, `memories sync` (opt-in hosted sync), `connect` and `disconnect`

The README also lists more subcommands, including `add`, `agent-guide`, `config`, `entities`, `show`, `memory`, `patterns`, `capabilities`, `version`, and `memories storage`. Run `entire brain --help` for their flags.

**Notes from the README:**

- Facts from a model can be wrong. Check their linked sources. `verify` checks source references, not whether conclusions are correct.
- Hand-written facts show as `unverifiable-here` in `verify`. This is expected.
- `recall` on a branch with no facts prints nothing. Pass `--branch main` before concluding that the brain knows nothing.
- Storage migration is one-way. Older Brain versions (v0.2.0 through v0.4.0) cannot read a migrated local store.
- Semantic (embedding) search was removed in favor of BM25.

Full docs are in the repo's `docs/` folder, including `reference.md` (the complete command reference), `operations.md` (install options), and `privacy`-related sections of the reference. I did not fetch those pages. Links to the reference and other docs appear on the README page.

I summarized the README rather than quoting it, because the page came from a non-preapproved source. Only the install and command strings are reproduced exactly. Source: https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain (read the README page on `main`).
